outlier: Highlights from Haskell Weekly Issue 447: Competitive Programming, ICFP 2024, and GHC 9.12.1-alpha3

recent_posts.title: Issue 522
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 522 covers a range of community news and articles. Featured content includes a token efficiency comparison between Haskell and Python notebooks, a project recap for the Botan cryptography bindings, a podcast episode with DB systems professor Torsten Grust on compiling to SQL, and a post arguing functional programmers should look at Zig's comptime. Other highlights include Pure Borrow bringing Rust-style borrowing to Linear Haskell, a Simon Peyton Jones interview on Haskell and Verse, monad explainers, and a Scheme-vs-Haskell opinion piece. Brief items include the Clash 1.10 hardware description language release, a new Haskell debugger v0.13, and a Nix-inspired test caching tool. Community calls include MuniHac 2026 registration and a GHC proposal for redundant commas.

recent_posts.title: Issue 521
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 521 covers several community highlights: a video on selective functors as an alternative to monads and applicative functors, a post on achieving a 5x speedup in the xreferee linter using elemIndex, a comparison of Haskell vs R and Pandas for data exploration, and a guide to writing a WebSocket server for a turn-based game. Brief items include Ghcitty (an enhanced GHCi with syntax highlighting and Hoogle integration), haskell-flake 1.0.0 (now decoupled from flake-parts), and stm-ringbuffer (a fixed-size STM ring buffer outperforming TBQueue). Community show-and-tell features Lawvere theory encodings in Haskell and a Brick TUI dashboard driven by Nix files.

recent_posts.title: Issue 520
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 520 curates community content including: a post on making code differentiable with a simple switch, a POPL 2026 podcast episode, a Haskell data visualization tutorial covering interactivity and small multiples, a JSON parser walkthrough, a story about building pGenie (a SQL-first Postgres code generator after abandoning ORMs), a deep dive into property-based testing concepts, and a Functor/Foldable typeclass tutorial. Brief items include the first release of hs-wayland-scanner, a GHCup 0.2.0.0 RC enabling arbitrary tool installation, a discussion on GHC STM internals, and a lightweight enumeration-based property testing library. Show & tell highlights Hatter (native Haskell mobile apps for Android/iOS) and Rivulet (a Wayland compositor in Haskell).

recent_posts.title: Issue 519
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 519 covers the latest news and releases in the Haskell community. Featured articles include a deep dive into tensor corepresentation with type-level arithmetic, a discussion of Haskell's re-export module pattern, the miso v1.9.0 release introducing React-style components with type-safe message-passing, and a post on type-level programming for typed dataframe APIs. Brief items include a new composable HTTP middleware library inspired by Rust's Tower, Scarf's open-sourced ClickHouse client, and the Skeletest 0.4.0 test framework release. There's also a job posting for a Haskell hardware design engineer at MatX.

recent_posts.title: Issue 518
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 518 covers a range of community news and articles. Highlights include a detailed production engineering post from Mercury about running millions of lines of Haskell at scale in fintech, the release of GHC 9.12.4, a March 2026 GHC community update, a tutorial on the Traversable typeclass for Elm developers, and a project on writing an OS in Haskell. Shorter items include a new CSS class bindings library, an AI-friendly Haskell minifier (HSMin), a Bézier toolkit package, and pGenie, a SQL-first code generator for PostgreSQL. The show-and-tell section features a second alpha of hs-bindgen for automatic Haskell-C FFI bindings.

recent_posts.title: Issue 517
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 517 covers community news including the loss and recovery of the newsletter subscriber list, an opinion piece arguing against currying in favor of tuple-style function application, the release of dataframe 1.0.0.0 after two years of development, a podcast episode with professor Peter Thiemann on Haskell's early history and type system innovations, Well-Typed's Q1 2026 ecosystem activities report covering GHC/Cabal/HLS work, a deep dive into the perils of MonadBaseControl, the major IHP v1.5 release with a complete database layer rewrite, a new type-safe PostgreSQL library pg-schema, and a book announcement for Haskell Brain Teasers.

recent_posts.title: Issue 516
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 516 covers a range of community news and resources. Featured content includes a refresher on the IO Monad, a discussion on value representation in functional languages vs Java's Valhalla project, a GHC 9.12.4 release candidate announcement, and a two-week Haskell onboarding curriculum used for new engineering hires. Brief items include a fork of the memory library (ram), a new type-safe primitive conversion library (unwitch), and an OpenCode API client for Haskell. Community highlights feature a new Flexible Haskell plugin for JetBrains IDEs and Sabela reactive notebooks. A reminder is also included about the approaching Google Summer of Code deadline for Haskell projects.

recent_posts.title: Issue 515
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly issue 515 curates community news including: a personal static site generator built over 11 months using literate programming; a podcast episode on teaching Haskell at university level; two contrasting takes on LLMs with Haskell (one positive, one skeptical); a free interactive Haskell learning tool for high school students; a sneak peek at a new math library; announcements for Scrod (a faster Haddock alternative), temporary-ospath, and doubly-linked lists in Haskell; a community update to 'Learn You a Haskell'; and a call for papers for the Functional Software Architecture Workshop at ICFP 2026.

recent_posts.title: Issue 514
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 514 covers the latest in the Haskell community including featured content on lazy evaluation, Church encoding in lambda calculus, monus-based heap algorithms, the Sabela reactive notebook prototype, and the State of Haskell 2025 survey results. New releases highlighted include SBV v13.6 for SMT-based verification, Brillo 2.0 for 2D graphics, beam-duckdb, vscode-haskell 2.8.0, and Layoutz 0.3.2. Job listings for Haskell engineers at Habito and Mercury are also included.

recent_posts.title: Haskell Weekly issue 513 community roundup
recent_posts.summary: Haskell Weekly Issue 513 curates the latest news and releases from the Haskell community. Featured content includes benchmarking LLM proficiency with Advent of Code puzzles in Haskell, a podcast episode on functional programming in industry, a web-based heap visualizer for ghc-debug, a tutorial on the Foldable typeclass for Elm developers, a guide to efficient PostgreSQL integration in Haskell, and a DSL for Template Haskell AST construction. Brief announcements cover releases of Stack 3.9.3, a new Haskell debugger v0.12, cassava 0.5.5.0, esqueleto-postgis v4, kdl-hs 1.0.0, a reactive Haskell notebook called sabela, and Haskell.org's acceptance into Google Summer of Code 2026.
